title: Sensors
subject: Computer Science
description: What a sensor is, what sensors are used for, the 8 key types, the ADC, and how control systems work.
author: Erick

cards.back: An input device which detects or measures a physical property.
Using a sensor to measure and record physical data of the environment around it, e.g. a scientist taking readings for an experiment.

cards.front: How can sensors be used to control systems?
cards.back: They detect and measure changes in the environment around the sensor to control a system, e.g. a security system detecting motion to trigger a burglar alarm.

cards.front: How do sensors help an input device work?
cards.back: They detect and measure changes in the environment around the sensor to enable the input device to work, e.g. sensors in a games controller.

cards.front: What are the three uses of sensors?
cards.back:
1. Measure and record physical data (data logging)
2. Detect and measure changes to control systems
3. Detect and measure changes to enable an input device to work

cards.front: Name the 8 key types of sensor
cards.back: Light, temperature, motion, magnetic field, gas, pressure, moisture and pH sensors.
Analogue-to-digital convertor: converts an analogue signal into a digital signal (1s and 0s).

cards.front: How does a sensor's reading get into a computer?
cards.back: The sensor produces an analogue signal, an ADC converts it into digital data, and the computer (or microprocessor) then processes it.

cards.front: How does a sensor-based control system work?
cards.back: Sensors take readings, which are converted to digital by an ADC. The microprocessor compares each reading with a preset value. If it's outside the range, it sends a signal (via a DAC if needed) to an actuator, e.g. to switch on a heater. This repeats continuously.

cards.front: What is the difference between data logging and a control system?
cards.back: Data logging only measures and records readings. A control system also acts on the readings, using actuators to change the environment.
